### Complete Assurance for Incomplete People
Author: John Piper
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/complete-assurance-for-incomplete-people
Passage: Hebrews 10:14
Points:
- Christ’s single sacrifice has already perfected believers before the Father for all time.
- Being perfected does not imply moral flawlessness or an end to sin in this earthly life.
- In this passage, perfection means full forgiveness where God never counts our sins against us.
- Believers live in the reality of already being perfected while simultaneously undergoing sanctification.
- Lingering weakness is not disqualification, but motivates moving away from sin toward greater holiness.

### You Only Need to Be Saved Once
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-september-20-2026.html
Passage: Hebrews 10:14
Points:
- Scripture never records anyone needing to be saved more than once.
- Christ made one all-sufficient offering that permanently secures those being sanctified.
- Requiring repeated salvation would falsely imply that Jesus must return to die again.
- Believers can rest with full assurance in the permanent security purchased at the cross.

### Dress in White
Author: Lisa Morrone
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/girlfriends/girlfriends-in-god-march-10-2020.html
Passage: Hebrews 10:14
Points:
- Justification occurs instantly at conversion, clothing the believer in pure spiritual garments.
- Old Testament sacrifices offered temporary external covering, whereas Jesus permanently cleansed the heart.
- Sanctification is the daily process of walking carefully to avoid the defilement of sin.
- When believers stumble, prompt confession and repentance restore clean fellowship with God.

### Redemption through His Blood
Author: Oswald Chambers
Site: Utmost.org
URL: https://utmost.org/modern-classic/redemption-through-his-blood/
Passage: Hebrews 10:14
Points:
- Divine forgiveness is grounded entirely in the cross of Christ, not in human sorrow or tears.
- No amount of human pleading or moral striving can earn standing before God.
- True salvation requires humbling oneself to enter through the single door of Christ's sacrifice.
- Through Christ's atonement, God actively transforms unholy sinners into holy people.
